parole.testo: From Middle Persian ʾwʾz (āwāč, āwāz, “voice, sound, tune”), from 𐭥𐭠𐭰 (wāč, wāz, “word, speech”), from Proto-Iranian *wā́xš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wā́kš, from Proto-Indo-European *wōkʷs. Cognate with Sanskrit वाच् (vā́c) and Latin vōx.

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾlcʾn /⁠arzān⁠/), 𐫀𐫡𐫉𐫀𐫗 (ʾrzʾn /⁠arzān⁠/, “valuable, worthy”), from [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾlc /⁠arz⁠/, “worth, value”) + [Book Pahlavi needed] (-ʾn /⁠-ān⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *Hárǰ-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hárǰʰ- (“to be worth”). Cognate with Parthian
From ارز (arz-, present stem of ارزیدن (arzidan, “to be worth”)) + ـش (-eš). From Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hargʰás (“price, value”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂elgʷʰ-ós. Cognate with Ossetian аргъ (arǧ).
Old derivation from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kar- (“to do, make”), whence also کردن (kardan), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷer-.

From Middle Persian 𐭲𐭠𐭥 (tʾr /⁠tār⁠/, “darkness”), from Proto-Iranian *támHsram, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *támHsram, from Proto-Indo-European *temH-. Cognate to Avestan 𐬙𐬄𐬚𐬭𐬀 (tąθra), Pashto تور (tor, “black”), Sanskrit तमिस्र (tamisra), Latin tenebrae.
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *trāsás, from Proto-Indo-European *tros-ó-s (“fear, dread”), from *tres- (“to tremble (with fear)”). Compare Sanskrit त्रास (trāsa).

Per Derksen, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kʰād-, from Proto-Indo-European *k(ʷ)end- or *k(ʷ)enHd(ʰ)-. Compare Sanskrit खाद् (khād) and खादति (khādati, “to chew, to bite”), Ancient Greek κνώδων (knṓdōn, “sword, spear spikes”) and Khotanese khays- (“to drink”).
Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *krā́mHti.

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (hlt /⁠xrat, xrad⁠/, “wisdom, understanding, intelligence”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *krátuš (“intelligence, mental power”), from Proto-Indo-European *krét-us. Akin to Old Armenian խրատ (xrat), an Iranian borrowing.
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *swaćrúH, from Proto-Indo-European *sweḱrúh₂ (“mother-in-law”). Compare Sanskrit श्वश्रू (śvaśrū).
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *dáHma (compare Sanskrit दामन् (dā́man, “string, cord, rope, fetter”)), from Proto-Indo-European *déh₁-mn̥, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₁- (“to bind”).

Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭲𐭥𐭩𐭭 (tʿyn /⁠dō⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *dwáH, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dwáH, from Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁. Indo European cognates include Northern Kurdish du, Northern Luri دوو (doo), Pashto دوه (dwa), Avestan 𐬛𐬎𐬎𐬀 (duua), Sanskrit द्व (dvá), Hindi दो (do) / Urdu دو
Perhaps from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrā́ćš.

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (lwd), 𐫡𐫇𐫏 (rwy /⁠rōy⁠/, “copper, brass”), Northern Luri ڕوویی (rruyi), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrawdáh (“copper, brass”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrawdʰás.

From a Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?] root shared with Sanskrit जू (jū, “hurry on, hurry, be quick”), Avestan 𐬰𐬆𐬬𐬍𐬱𐬙𐬫𐬀 (zəvīštya, “the quickest”), and Northern Kurdish zû, Northern Luri زی (zi), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *ǵewH- (“force, drive”) and thus further cognate with Proto-Slavic *žuriti

From Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćyaHmás (“black”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱyeh₁-mó-s (“black, dark”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱeh₃- (“darkness, shadow”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬯𐬁𐬨𐬀 (sāma, “black”), Sanskrit श्याम (śyāma). Related to سیاه (siyâh, “black”), and سیاوش (siyâvaš).
From Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?]; cognate to Sanskrit शाण (śāṇa, “whetstone”).

Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćā́kʰaH, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱókh₂eh₂ (“branch”). From Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćā́kʰaH, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱókh₂eh₂ (“branch”). parole.significato: to become; a light verb used in a large number of intransitive compound verbs.
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (OZLWN-tn' /⁠šudan⁠/), from Old Persian 𐎠𐏁𐎡𐎹𐎺𐎶 (š(i)yav-, “to set, go forth”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čyáwatay, from Proto-Indo-European *kyew- (“to move, go”). Cognates include Northern Kurdish çûn (“to go”), Ossetian цӕуын (cæwyn), Pashto شول (šwəl),
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *kubȷ́ás, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱewb-, see also Sanskrit कुब्ज (kubja), Latin cubō, Old English hype.
Cognate to Iron Ossetian фынк (fynk), Digor Ossetian финкӕ (finkæ, “foam”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pʰáynas (“foam, froth”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)póHy-nh₂-os.

Inherited from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?], a suffixed form of Proto-Indo-European *lek- (“to bend, leg”). Cognate with Ancient Greek λάξ (láx, “with the leg/heel”), Ancient Greek λᾰκτῐ́ζω (lăktĭ́zō, “to kick”); Sanskrit लकुट (lakuṭa, “stick, club”); Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀮𑀢𑁆𑀢𑀸 (lattā, “kick”), the latte
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *mr̥táh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *mr̥tás, from Proto-Indo-European *mr̥tós, from *mer- (“to die”).

Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭬𐭮𐭲 (mst /⁠mast⁠/, “drunk, bemused”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *matˢtás (“drunk, intoxicated”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“wet”). Cognate with Sanskrit मत्त (matta).

Ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *muktás (whence also زمخت (zumuxt)), from Proto-Indo-European *muk-tó-s (“released, discharged”), from *(s)mewk- (“to free, escape”). Compare Sanskrit मुक्त (mukta) or मोक्ष् (mokṣ).
Derived from the word مور (mur, “ant”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *marwíš.
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *ná (“no, not”).

Formed with a base ultimately going back to Proto-Indo-Iranian *náyȷ́žʰam. Akin to Middle Iranian borrowings: Old Armenian նիշտր (ništr), նշտրակ (nštrak), and Classical Syriac ܐܫܬܪܟܐ (/⁠ˀštrkˀ⁠/) to be emended to ܢܫܬܪܟܐ* (/⁠*nštrkˀ⁠/).
Perhaps from Proto-Indo-Iranian *sádaH (“always”). Compare Sanskrit सदा (sadā, “always”), Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬜𐬀 (haδa, “always”).
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *(s)káras, from Proto-Iranian *(s)káras, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kʷálos. Compare Avestan 𐬐𐬀𐬭𐬀 (kara, “kind of fish”). Distant cognate with English whale.
From Proto-Indo-Iranian *pā́ršniš, from Proto-Indo-European *tpḗrsneh₂.

parole.significato: old, aged (of living things; see also قدیمی (qadimi) for non-living things)
parole.testo: From Middle Persian 𐬞𐬌𐬭 (pyl /⁠pīr⁠/, “old, aged, ancient”), from Proto-Iranian *paru- (“ash-gray, pale gray, hoary”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *parHušás (“gray”); compare Sanskrit परुष (paruṣa, “spotted, rough”) and English pale.

Likely ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čálHati (“to move, to walk”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷélh₁-e-ti (“to turn”), although the regular descendant of this in Persian is چریدن (čaridan, “to graze”). Learned borrowing from Old Persian 𐎠𐎼𐎡𐎹 (a-r-i-y /⁠Aryaʰ⁠/) or Avestan 𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬋 (aⁱriiō), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Áryas (see for more information).
